# README Examples

Real-world READMEs worth studying. Each entry notes what makes it effective — use these as inspiration when deciding which elements to include.

## Patterns to borrow

| Pattern | When to use |
|---------|-------------|
| Project logo + banner | Libraries, apps with a visual identity |
| GIF demo | Any project with a UI or interactive CLI |
| Animated project banner | Open-source tools, high-visibility projects |
| Badges (CI, version, license) | Published packages, anything with a pipeline |
| TOC with anchor links | Long READMEs with 5+ sections |
| Collapsible sections | Detailed content that shouldn't bury the lede |
| Architecture diagram | Multi-service or non-obvious systems |
| Comparison table | Libraries competing with alternatives |
| Contributors/stargazers section | Community-oriented open-source projects |
| "Back to top" footer links | Long documentation-style READMEs |
